text:
marta: Heads up — working on a proposal for request/response logging defaults. want feedback before i open a PR.
jon: high level? sampling tiers or full-off by default?
sarah: tl;dr: we need safe default (minimal PII risk) + easy per-route opt-in for richer traces.
lee: agree. default should be 1% request sampling, 0% response bodies, but allow per-route full capture for debug.
marta: Proposal draft:
- global default sampling = 1% of requests (headers + latency + status)
- response body capture = off globally; route-level boolean `capture_response_bodies` opt-in for service owners
- when opt-in, auto-redact known PII fields unless owner marks route `pii-allowed` (requires security review)

jon: what counts as "known PII fields"? we need an explicit list and a sanitization strategy.
sarah: initial list: names, emails, phone numbers, national ids, credit card numbers, addresses. sanitize by tokenization (hash with salt) for identifiers, redact for free-form text blobs.
lee: hashing is fine for deterministic lookup but still considered PII by compliance unless salted per-customer. we should salt with route+env+org id.
marta: agreed. doc includes salted HMAC-256 approach for identifiers. free text redaction: run a lightweight NER model to mask tokens flagged as PII, then keep redaction metadata.
security-bot: FYI: any NER-based masking must have fallback: if confidence < 0.8, redact the entire field.
jon: console UX: owners need to enable route capture and see evidence of redaction inline. i propose a toggle in the route settings + preview window showing anonymized sample.
sarah: also need Audit log entry when `pii-allowed` is enabled. That should route to security and trigger a manual review step before retention policies change.
lee: retention: default logs kept 90 days for sampled data; full captures (route-level opt-ins) limited to 7 days unless approved for 30 via ticket.
marta: rollout plan:
1) feature flag `sampling_v2` disabled by default
2) enable for internal orgs + staging to validate sanitizers
3) open PR for console toggle + API param `capture_response_bodies`
4) 2-week opt-in window for each team before enforcement

jon: API details? want to avoid changing existing client shape. can we add an optional header `X-Redwood-Log-Mode: full|sample|none` that overrides sampling for that request and is audited?
sarah: header ok, but must only be honored for internal keys or dedicated capacity. hosted keys should ignore unless org has `capture_response_bodies` turned on.
lee: also need to throttle header-based overrides to prevent abuse; cap to 1000 requests/day/org.
marta: implementation notes in PR: pseudocode for sampling decision:
```
if header_override and org_allowed:
  decision = header_override
else:
  decision = route_override or global_sampling
```
redaction pipeline runs before persist.

jon: telemetry: we need new metrics: `logs.sampled.count`, `logs.redacted.count`, `logs.capture_requests.count` and latency impact gauge. include per-route labels.
sarah: add histograms for redaction CPU time — NER costs could be non-trivial.
lee: ops concern: backpressure if many routes enable full capture. should auto-reject capture toggles when cluster qps > threshold and provide a queued enable request.
marta: good call. console UX should surface capacity warnings and recommend burst capture windows.
security-bot: remember legal: some regions disallow export of certain identifiers. include region-based denylist for `capture_response_bodies`.
jon: outstanding: who signs off on `pii-allowed`? suggest security + legal + product owner. we need a small policy and checklist.
sarah: i'll draft checklist (data minimization, justified use case, retention justification, protections).
marta: i'll file the PR today with README and link to the checklist. tagging @lee @jon for review.
deploy-bot: deploy queued — shadow-sanitizer v0.3 to staging (sha: a1b2c3)
lee: quick smoke run on staging after deploy, i'll kick off load test against 10 routes.
jon: thanks — if staging looks good we can open a gradual rollout RFC for next week. :thumbsup:
